newsitem.title: FINLAND: GERMAN, FRENCH EMU DRIVE RISK FOR FINNISH GROWTH - PT.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN, FRENCH EMU DRIVE RISK FOR FINNISH GROWTH - PT.

text.p: The biggest cloud over 1997-98 growth prospects in Finland is weak demand for Finnish products in markets like Germany and France due to their public savings to reach fiscal criteria for EMU, a think-tank said on Monday.

Pekka Sauramo, head of research at the Labour Economic Research Institute (PT), told reporters that "the biggest risk" was that growth in key export countries, notably Germany and France, would fade in the run-up to a single European currency.
"It is possible that their efforts to reach the EMU criteria will force such savings operations that demand comes to a halt ... that the growth in our exports breaks," he said.

"The rate of export growth will remain high into 1998 always assuming that adjustment to the EMU criteria does not halt economic revival in Germany and France," the institute said in a report released on Monday.
The institute's Finnish exports growth forecast was seven percent this year, and six per cent for 1998.
